value.body: An MS by Research (often written MS (R)) is a master's degree in engineering offered by IITs, IISc and some other institutes. Unlike a coursework-heavy M.Tech, it centres on a research thesis under a faculty guide, with a smaller set of courses. Graduates move into R&D roles, a PhD, or industry work that values research experience.

items.label: Duration
items.note: No fixed end date at many institutes; it finishes when the thesis is accepted

items.label: Where it is offered
items.value: IITs, IISc and some NITs / IIITs
items.note: Called MS (Research) at IITs; IISc runs a similar M.Tech (Research)

items.label: Assistantship
items.note: Half-time teaching or research assistantship for eligible full-time GATE-qualified scholars at many IITs; rules vary

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.E. / B.Tech in a related branch, usually with a valid GATE score for a stipend. Each institute shortlists applicants and then holds a written test and / or interview with the department. Some institutes also admit sponsored candidates from industry or government labs.

value.title: At a glance
items: The thesis is the main output, so the choice of guide and lab shapes the experience.
Some institutes allow an MS (R) scholar to upgrade to a PhD midway.
Admission is run by each department, often twice a year; deadlines and cut-offs differ.
It suits people who want research experience without committing to a full PhD at the start.
